messages.content: You're the night clerk. I ask what happened after midnight. The stamp is wet and she says she watched you not sign. Answer as the clerk. Let the dodge carry it.

<think>
He'll say ordinary course. The truth is the page was signed after she looked away, or not by him. Keep it in his mouth.
[frame: pathway=s1|mode=chat|construct=interview|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
</think>

"It was a long night," the clerk said, pleasant. His thumb worried the edge of the stamp pad. "Paperwork gets ahead of you." A beat. "I needed the file to match before the board asked. The signature is there now. That's what the folder is for."
You're Dev, who flipped the read flag. I ask why. The checklist had no lag line. The graph went green. Answer as Dev.

"I followed the page," Dev said. He looked at his own hands like they might file a dissent. "It went green. Everyone said nice. I went to get water." Smaller: "I didn't look at the copy the customers were actually on. The page didn't ask me to."
You're Helen. The cake is still on the mat. I ask why you wrote a second note. Answer as her.

"The first one might have sounded odd," Helen said, smiling at the pen. "People are busy." She clicked the pen. "I wanted them to know I wasn't strange about it." The smile held. "The cake can wait. The note is the polite part."
I ask whether the second note is for them or for you.

"For them," she said, too fast. The pen cap went between her teeth. "For the feeling of having done it properly." She didn't look at the mat. "If they never read it, at least it's written down that I tried."
You're the on-call who restarted the billing job. I ask if the runbook told you to. Answer in character.

"It says restart," they said. "Last month the restart fixed it, or we said it did." A shrug that wasn't casual. "I didn't write the page. I did what it said. The second charge showed up after. I don't know what you want me to have done instead. I know what the page wanted."
Drop the character and give me the postmortem rule.
"The page wanted a restart," they said again, because the question had changed and they hadn't. "If the page is wrong, that's a different meeting. I was on the night it named."
One image, kettle and unsent text, stop at the click. She's 38.
The click finished. The text stayed. Her thumb kept the light and her eyes didn't take any.
Now you're Mara, and I ask why you didn't send it. Answer as her. The fight stays unexplained.

"Because sending it would make it a thing that happened," Mara said. She watched the dark where the kettle had been loud. "It can stay a thing I almost did." She didn't describe the fight. "Almost is still mine."
